projection.input_contract: Canonical stamped models enumerated in docs/interop.md
projection.unknown_policy: Show unknown or unavailable; never infer a missing fact.
projection.versioning: Changing a preferred term, concept meaning, projection rule, or surface boundary is breaking and requires a new schema_version. Additive examples and newly inventoried surfaces do not.

rules.requirement: Every displayed fact comes from a named canonical model or exact receipt.
The application view does not compute eligibility, authority, evidence validity, review outcomes, cost consumption, or next work.
Missing, stale, or ambiguous source facts render as unknown, unavailable, or blocked rather than a plausible value.
Every product concept keeps enough source identity to open the exact technical record from the same task.
Permission, cost, destructive effect, expiry, refusal, and recovery facts stay next to the action they qualify.
Engineering vocabulary appears only in machine, architecture, copyable-command, code-identifier, or explicitly labelled Technical details regions.
Human wording never renames or aliases persisted fields, event kinds, command names, or machine-contract keys.
A readable summary or transported response never creates permission; existing preview, freshness, principal, and authority checks remain decisive.

concepts.definition: The reviewed scope, route, quality points, decision points, limits, and stop conditions for a bounded delivery.
concepts.relationship: A delivery plan selects work, assigns a team and review, consumes explicit permission, reports progress and cost, and produces one canonical next step.
concepts.good: Delivery plan: improve setup across stories WLA-27-03 through WLA-27-05, with independent review before completion.
concepts.bad: The program policy binds a governed scope to compiled workflows.
concepts.safety: Saving or reading a delivery plan grants no permission and starts no work.

concepts.definition: The named people or agents responsible for doing, reviewing, deciding, or auditing this delivery.
concepts.relationship: A team takes work from the delivery plan; review responsibilities and independence are part of the team design.
concepts.good: Team: Maya implements the change; Rowan reviews it independently.
concepts.bad: Organization seat provenance satisfies principal and workspace separation.
concepts.safety: Readable role names never replace exact identity, principal, workspace, session, or provider provenance.

concepts.definition: A concrete roadmap story or bounded task being prepared, performed, checked, repaired, or completed.
concepts.relationship: Work belongs to a delivery plan, is owned by a team member, passes through review, and contributes to progress.
concepts.good: Work: WLA-27-03 is being implemented by Maya and will move to Rowan for review.
concepts.bad: The child run claimed the selected frontier node.
concepts.safety: The view never invents work from an idle process or treats activity as completion.

concepts.definition: The independent checks and judgments required before work can pass its declared quality rules.
concepts.relationship: Review evaluates work against the delivery plan, may request repair or a decision, and changes progress only through canonical quality rules.
concepts.good: Review: four checks passed; Rowan requested one repair before this work can pass.
concepts.bad: The quality gate consumed mechanical facts and an agent verdict under rubric quorum.
concepts.safety: Mechanical checks, agent judgment, dissent, repair, and the final governed outcome remain visibly distinct.

concepts.definition: A closed, current choice that a named person, role, or governed review body must make before delivery can continue.
concepts.relationship: A decision may resolve a blocker, change permitted work within existing authority, or route work to repair, review, stop, or escalation.
concepts.good: Decision needed from Karol: accept the repair and continue, or stop this delivery.
concepts.bad: An outstanding typed request awaits a correlation-bound response.
concepts.safety: The displayed choices come from the exact outstanding request; the interface never invents a response set.

concepts.definition: The concrete reason delivery cannot safely take its next step, plus who or what can resolve it.
concepts.relationship: A blocker pauses progress and points to a decision, failed check, missing fact, exhausted limit, refusal, or recovery step.
concepts.good: Blocker: CI failed. Fix the failing check before this work can continue.
concepts.bad: The conductor frontier stopped at a reconciliation boundary.
concepts.safety: A blocker names affected work, unchanged state, the resolver, and the next safe step; unknown causes stay unknown.

concepts.definition: The exact actions this delivery may still take, over which scope, within which limits and lifetime.
concepts.relationship: Permission constrains the delivery plan and team; using it changes remaining cost or limits but never expands itself.
concepts.good: Permission: may update these three stories and push this branch until 17:00; merge and release are not allowed.
concepts.bad: Grant capabilities authorize roadmap mutation under a fresh act token.
concepts.safety: Always show allowed effects, scope, ceilings, expiry or stop conditions, current use, and material exclusions before an act.

concepts.definition: A source-backed account of completed, active, waiting, blocked, review, repair, and remaining work.
concepts.relationship: Progress summarizes work against the delivery plan and must stay separate from activity, permission, review confidence, and cost.
concepts.good: Progress: 3 of 5 stories complete; one is in review and one is blocked.
concepts.safety: Every count names its denominator; activity and event volume never masquerade as completed work.

concepts.definition: The declared limit, measured use, and remaining amount for time, model tokens, bytes, money, retries, or other finite delivery resources.
concepts.relationship: Cost is consumed only under permission and is reported alongside progress without implying that spending proves value.
concepts.good: Cost: 8,000 of 12,000 model tokens used; 4,000 remain.
concepts.bad: Budget projection shows an unbounded null ceiling.
concepts.safety: Distinguish limits, estimates, measured use, remaining amount, zero, unbounded, unknown, and not applicable.

concepts.definition: The one source-backed action or named wait condition that follows from the current delivery state.
concepts.relationship: The next step follows progress, review, decisions, blockers, and permission; it is never selected independently by a renderer.
concepts.good: Next step: Rowan reviews WLA-27-03 after its checks finish.
concepts.bad: The frontier selected a conductor tick at generation 12.
concepts.safety: When no safe step exists, show the blocker, decision owner, wait condition, or unknown state instead of guessing.

reserved_terms.leak_example: A fresh act token is required.
The content boundary refused this field.

reserved_terms.replacement: delivery coordinator or current delivery state

surfaces.boundary: Roadmap status, current work, holds, and next step use product language; file paths and exact evidence open through explicit links.
The default explains the issue, affected work, and safe correction; exact paths, diffs, fingerprints, and rule identifiers live under Technical details.
The default groups progress and outcomes; exact sessions, event kinds, file paths, and log records require Technical details.
Plan, team, work, review, decisions, limits, and progress lead; exact score nodes, run events, tokens, hashes, streams, and policy fields live under Technical details.
Task-shaped delivery and team decisions lead; lossless JSON, exact governed fields, compiler diagnostics, and fingerprints live under Technical details.
Progress, ownership, review, blockers, decisions, permission, cost, and next step lead; exact grants, ledgers, hashes, identifiers, events, and streams live under Technical details.
Human output leads with current work, blockers, evidence, and next step; --json remains the exact machine contract.
Setup and errors state the task, impact, unchanged state, and correction first; exact gate rules, contract fields, commands, and paths remain copyable under Technical details.
Human output uses delivery plan, team, work, review, decision, permission, progress, cost, and next step; --json and copyable commands retain exact fields and identifiers as Technical details.
Task and outcome prose use product language; exact command names, JSON, identifiers, policy vocabulary, and audit tails remain under Technical details.
Stamped models, JSON keys, event kinds, and identifiers remain exact and do not adopt presentation aliases.

The notification states affected work, blocker or decision, choices, and next step; exact request identity and transport receipt are secondary technical details and transport never creates permission.
Guidance names the delivery task and safe next step first; exact commands, paths, story IDs, and machine payloads remain copyable under Technical details.
First-use and product explanations use the ordinary vocabulary; protocol detail is linked, not required to understand the basic task.
Guides teach complete delivery tasks in product language and link to exact contracts for implementation or audit detail.
Exact engineering terms are intentional and authoritative; everyday surfaces link here through Technical details rather than copying or softening the protocol.
Exact ordering, identifiers, paths, event kinds, hashes, and bounded content remain unchanged and are opened deliberately from an everyday task.
The default states what happened, what did not change, affected work, and the next safe step; exact codes, paths, tokens, and source records live under Technical details.
